soundness_flags.label: ass:positive-bounded-directed-lags
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Jahn--Karnik--Schulman model permits contemporaneous directed edges and bounds both directed and bidirected latency, so it does not support the tagged strictly-positive-directed-lag condition.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:factorization-safe-quotient
soundness_flags.one_line: The question invokes a quotient of unspecified “raw global response signatures”; define that signature set, its quotient map, and the induced factorized image before asking for exact preservation.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Directed edges satisfy t≤t′, explicitly allowing contemporaneous edges; latency L bounds the absolute time difference of both directed and bidirected edges.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1578, Definition of possible parents and Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines possible parents over a known maximal lag and identifies the controlled micro direct effect by conditional-mean adjustment when Y has no nontrivial directed cycle and no bidirected edge to an ancestor.
The article presents an automated numerical approach reducing discrete causal questions to polynomial programs and numerically computing sharp bounds.
The reduced LP quotient preserves sharp bounds by pushing an unrestricted signature-simplex distribution forward and lifting each quotient mass uniformly over its class.
The proposition proves equality of full and reduced LP extrema when the linear objective and constraints factor through a quotient push-forward map on a simplex.
The paper derives analytically computable causal-effect bounds from a Partial Ancestral Graph representing a Markov-equivalence class.
The paper constructs finite-sample confidence regions for a multinomial parameter and relates them to confidence intervals for linear functionals.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the strict positive-lag restriction as a deliberate modelling restriction with an applied justification, or replace its citation with one that explicitly assumes no instantaneous directed effects; state separately whether bidirected lags are bounded.
Define a finite raw-signature domain and an explicit quotient/push-forward map for QCan, then make the A↔B↔C witness test an executable first theorem or a precisely quantified alternative branch.

Promote the temporal-instrument strictness result by giving the exact graph, response tables, and dual certificates as a reusable worked instance, rather than only numerical endpoints in a theorem target.

recommended_next_step: Revise the unsupported lag assumption and formalize the quotient object, then advance the field-tier sharp-envelope and strict-separation kernel to Stage 0.
